chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And mention Allah during the numbered days.' He said: 'The Takbeer (exclaiming Allahu Akbar) is during the Days of Tashreeq, from the Dhuhr prayer on the Day of Sacrifice until the Fajr prayer on the third day. And in the cities (AmSar), [it is for] ten prayers. So when the people leave after the first [day], the people of the cities cease [the Takbeer], and whoever stays in Mina and prays Dhuhr and Asr there, let him exclaim Takbeer.'
ai.seo_question: When does the Takbeer of Tashreeq begin and end according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the jurisprudential details of the Takbeer al-Tasbih, specifying that the obligatory recitation occurs during the ten prayers from Dhuhr on Eid al-Adha to Fajr on the 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah. It highlights the Shia distinction that while pilgrims in Mina continue the recitation, residents of other cities (Amsar) cease after the first day's prayers, reflecting the specific application of the verse 'And remember Allah during the numbered days' (2:203).

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘Abu Abdullahasws about the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [2:203] And mention Allah during the numbered days. Heasws said: ‘The exclamations of Takbeer during the days of Al-Tashreek (11th, 12th & 13th Zilhajj), from Salaat Al-Zohr from the day of the sacrifice up to the Salaat Al-Fajr from the third day, and in the cities there are ten Salaats. So when (the people) leave after the first (day), the people of the city would withhold (the Takbeer), and the one who stays in Mina, so he Prays in it Al-Zohr, and Al-Asr, so let him exclaim Takbeer’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said

the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, ‘Speak of Allah during the well identified days.’ [2:203] He (the Imam) said, ‘Takbir (Allah is great beyond description) during the bright days should be commenced at noontime on the tenth of Dhu al-Hajjah up to the morning of the 13th of Dhu al-Hajjah. In the cities however, it is during the ten salawat (prayers). As soon as people begin to leave Mina, people of the cities discontinue Takbirat (Allah is great beyond description); however, people who still remain in Mina’ must say Zuhr and al-‘Asr salat (prayer) and al-Takbirat (Allah is great beyond description) there.”’
